rules.statement: When the token endpoint finds an authorization code was already redeemed, deny the request and revoke all grants for the code's end-user session (the session grant plus access- and refresh-token grants issued under it).
rules.why: RFC 6749 §4.1.2 and RFC 9700 treat a second redemption as a compromise signal, and tokens issued from the code should be revoked; the session is the only server-side handle for revoking self-contained JWTs.
rules.check: Look for code-redemption logic that rejects an already-consumed code without also starting session-scoped revocation by sid.

rules.statement: Code-replay revocation must not trigger user-logout side effects such as logout auditing or back-channel logout as if the user had logged out; it is a security revocation, not a user-initiated logout.
rules.why: The ADR separates a security revocation from a user-initiated logout. ADR-0228 later amended this: a replayed code now terminates its session through the termination seam, which notifies the session's relying parties and audits the termination.
rules.check: Check that the replay path does not call the user-logout flow directly. Any notification or audit should go through the session-termination seam.

rules.statement: Always put the end-user session identifier (`sid`, RFC 9068 §2.2.1) in subject-bound access tokens, and do not make it a per-client opt-in setting.
rules.why: Session binding is a security property that cannot be bypassed, and revocation enforcement depends on it.
rules.check: Look for conditional emission of the sid claim in access tokens, or client settings that turn it on or off.

rules.statement: Every first-party endpoint that authenticates a self-issued access token (such as UserInfo, introspection and management APIs) must resolve the token's `sid` and reject the token with `invalid_token`/401 when that session is revoked, using the shared token-validation seam.
rules.why: Without this check, tokens issued under a revoked or compromised session stay usable at the OP's own endpoints, and the conformance suite expects a 4xx after a code replay.
rules.check: Look for new or changed endpoints that accept the server's own access tokens but only validate the JWT signature and lifetime, with no session-status check.

rules.statement: Do not add a global access-token denylist, reference tokens, or per-access-token server state just for revocation; revoke by session instead.
rules.why: Per-token state and a lookup on every call bring back the cost that stateless JWTs exist to avoid.
rules.check: Look for new stores or tables that record issued access-token identifiers for revocation, or denylist lookups.
